scope: HPA heart muscle samples 149-152 (4 donors); 2 annotated CTAG2 transcripts
finding: The epitope-containing isoform is present in heart, not just the epitope-lacking one. LAGE-1A (ENST00000369585 = UniProt O75638-2, the only CTAG2 isoform carrying SLLMWITQC) is estimated in both RNA-positive heart-muscle samples, at 44.7% (sample 149) and 37.4% (sample 152) of summed CTAG2 transcript TPM; samples 150 and 151 are zero for both transcripts. The heart signal is therefore not attributable solely to LAGE-1B (ENST00000247306 = O75638-1), which lacks the epitope.
limitations: Computational transcript-abundance estimates over two annotated transcripts; not validated by splice-junction or long-read evidence. Does not identify the expressing cell type and does not establish peptide-HLA presentation.

scope: HPA v23 heart muscle (4 donors); GTEx v10 heart atrial appendage and left ventricle
finding: The heart signal is donor-restricted rather than uniform low-level expression. 2 of 4 HPA v23 heart-muscle donors are positive (13.5 and 7.1 nTPM) and 2 are zero, producing the 5.1 nTPM consensus. GTEx v10 agrees in shape: median 0 TPM in both heart regions, with 15 of 461 atrial appendage and 16 of 452 left ventricle donors at or above 1 TPM and maxima of 19.9 and 41.2 TPM.
limitations: Bulk tissue: a positive donor does not localize signal to cardiomyocytes. HPA IHC and RNA donors are different individuals, so the RNA/IHC discordance cannot be resolved within a donor. GTEx and HPA use different quantification pipelines and units.

scope: HPA v23 single-cell heart, 2 datasets (40,388 and 11,505 cells)
finding: Single-cell data do not localize the bulk heart signal to any cell type. 1 nonzero observation out of 40,388 cells in the first dataset (cardiomyocyte cluster c-3, 0.152713 normalized) and 0 of 11,505 in the second, across 33,023 and 7,205 cardiomyocytes respectively.
limitations: Shallow droplet-based coverage: a single count neither establishes nor excludes low-level or donor-restricted expression. These donors are not the RNA-positive bulk donors, so absence here does not contradict the bulk measurement.

source_version: FDA TECELRA prescribing information; lete-cel NSCLC primary report
finding: Afami-cel (TECELRA; SPEARHEAD-1) targets MAGE-A4, not CTAG2/NY-ESO-1. Lete-cel recognizes the HLA-A*02-presented SLLMWITQC epitope shared by NY-ESO-1 and LAGE-1A.
limitations: Afami-cel safety outcomes cannot establish CTAG2 cardiac safety; recognition of a shared epitope does not establish its presentation in heart.

scope: Robbins NY-ESO-1 TCR trials (2011 and 2015 follow-up)
finding: The 2011 and 2015 reports attribute no toxicities to the transferred NY-ESO-1-reactive cells. The 2015 follow-up nevertheless reports a treatment-related death from E. coli septic shock during neutropenia, three days after transfer.
limitations: The follow-up overlaps the original cohort and is not independent replication. These reports do not establish absence of rare cardiac toxicity or CTAG2 peptide-HLA in heart; conditioning and IL-2 also cause toxicity.

scope: Lete-cel MRCLS pilot NCT02992743; 20 infused patients
finding: One potentially treatment-related fatal cardiac arrest occurred on day 161 after lete-cel, after disease progression, with hypotension from poor oral intake, renal insufficiency, and intervening radiation/pazopanib for a new spine metastasis. A blanket claim of no cardiac events is incorrect.
limitations: This confounded adverse event does not demonstrate on-target CTAG2-mediated cardiomyocyte injury or peptide presentation.

scope: Lete-cel program safety review; NCT03709706 protocol Table 9 and section 2.3.2
finding: Table 9 records two unexpected fatal cardiac arrests: one at about five months with hypotension/renal insufficiency and another at about one week with recent fungal line infection, caspofungin, and pneumonia/edema. The day-161 case also had early grade 3 CRS with supraventricular tachycardia/hypotension; investigator and sponsor causality assessments differed.
limitations: Program-level cases overlap trial reports and must not be summed as independent events. Confounders and discordant attribution leave causality unresolved; these are not proof of CTAG2 expression in cardiomyocytes.

finding: Linette et al. reported fatal cardiac toxicity from an affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 TCR with titin-peptide cross-reactivity. This is a different receptor and antigen from NY-ESO-1/LAGE-1.
limitations: The precedent establishes a receptor-specific off-target risk, not evidence that CTAG2 protein is expressed in heart or that all TCR constructs share this risk.
